Acquisition Log 2017
Acquisition log

----------------------------------------------------------------------
002 | HM-2017-002 | 2017-01-17 | PUR
Specimen: Collection of 14 mounted insect specimens, order Lepidoptera, mixed genera, in original Riker mounts.
Source: Estate sale of Dr. Arnold P. Fielding, conducted by Brigham Auction House, Ann Arbor, Michigan.
Remarks: Purchased with funds from the Fielding Memorial Endowment. Lot 44. Mounts dated 1950s–1970s. Labels legible; some pin damage. Condition C. No export or permit issues; domestic sale.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
003 | HM-2017-003 | 2017-01-23 | XFR
Specimen: Fossil leaf compression, Alethopteris sp., from the Mazon Creek flora.
Source: Transfer from the Department of Geology, State University of Illinois, per deaccession agreement dated 2016-12-15.
Remarks: Received in exchange for loan of type material. Original field number MC-221. Locality: Pit 11, Will County, Illinois. Condition B. Transfer paperwork complete.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
004 | HM-2017-004 | 2017-02-02 | DON
Specimen: Small box of mixed shell fragments, marine gastropods and bivalves, unlabeled.
Donor: Mr. Thomas R. Evers, of Toledo, Ohio.
Remarks: Donor stated the shells were collected by his grandfather along the Gulf Coast of Florida, likely in the 1930s. No precise locality. Offered without conditions. Condition C. Retained for educational use; not suitable for research.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
005 | HM-2017-005 | 2017-02-14 | LEG
Specimen: Framed plaster relief of a trilobite, Elrathia kingii, with handwritten label "Wheeler Shale, Utah."
Source: Bequest of Ms. Clara B. Dennison, of Kalamazoo, Michigan. Estate settled by Dennison & Sons Law Office.
Remarks: Received with a small archive of field notebooks (see accession file). Relief is a teaching replica, not an original fossil. Condition B. The notebooks are catalogued separately under Archives.

Specimen #HM-2017-034 acquisition_date 2017-04-12 date. Record status: current.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
006 | HM-2017-006 | 2017-02-21 | PUR
Specimen: Three mineral specimens, including one terminated smoky quartz crystal, one amazonite, and one fluorite octahedron.
Source: Purchased from Mrs. Yvonne Delacroix, private collector, via online sale.
Remarks: Seller provided original collection labels from the 1980s. Localities listed as Pike's Peak region (amazonite), and unknown for quartz and fluorite. Condition A. Payment processed via purchase order 2017-118.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
007 | HM-2017-007 | 2017-03-03 | DON
Specimen: Taxidermy mount of a red fox (Vulpes vulpes), adult male, in standing pose.
Donor: Mr. Gerald T. Whitfield, of Battle Creek, Michigan.
Remarks: Mount was displayed in the donor's family cabin for approximately 40 years. Some fur loss on the tail; base is loose. Condition C. Donor asked that the mount be used for educational programs if possible. No CITES concerns for domestic red fox.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
008 | HM-2017-008 | 2017-03-11 | XFR
Specimen: Series of 5 fossil brachiopod slabs, Spirifer sp., from the Devonian of central New York.
Source: Transfer from the Paleontological Research Institution, Ithaca, New York.
Remarks: Received on permanent loan, not ownership. See loan agreement L-2017-04. Slabs are part of a teaching set formerly used at a field camp. Condition B.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
011 | HM-2017-011 | 2017-04-19 | PUR
Specimen: Two mounted deer antlers (white-tailed deer), one matched pair and one single antler.
Source: Purchased from Mr. Arnold J. Beeler, of Traverse City, Michigan.
Remarks: Antlers are from a private collection and were cleaned and bleached prior to sale. Pair shows slight asymmetry; single antler has a broken tine. Condition C. Purchase order 2017-146. Donor had no additional locality data; likely from northern Lower Peninsula.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
012 | HM-2017-012 | 2017-05-01 | DON
Specimen: Cast of a Dunkleosteus skull, Late Devonian, from the Cleveland Shale.
Donor: Dr. Raymond T. Oberlin, Professor Emeritus, Department of Geology, Michigan State University.
Remarks: Cast is in good condition with minor paint wear on the snout. Original specimen housed at the Cleveland Museum of Natural History. Donated to support the museum's paleontology education programs. Condition B. Cast number 14 of 25.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
013 | HM-2017-013 | 2017-05-14 | XFR
Specimen: Six framed geological survey maps of Michigan, published between 1910 and 1935.
Source: Transfer from the State Archives of Michigan, Lansing, Michigan.
Remarks: Maps are printed on heavy paper and show county boundaries, mineral deposits, and early road networks. One map has a tear along the fold; all others are intact. Condition C. Transfer approved under T-2017-18. Maps to be stored flat in map case 3.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
014 | HM-2017-014 | 2017-05-27 | DON
Specimen: Small collection of 8 glass-plate negatives depicting Michigan lumber camps, circa 1890–1905.
Donor: Ms. Ruth A. Lindquist, of Saginaw, Michigan.
Remarks: Negatives were found in the attic of the donor's family home. Subjects include logging crews, a steam donkey, and camp buildings. Plates are in original wooden boxes with tissue interleaving. Condition B; one plate has a chipped corner. To be digitized and catalogued under the photography collection.

Specimen #HM-2019-102 acquisition_date 2019-08-23 date. Record status: current.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
015 | HM-2017-015 | 2017-06-09 | PUR
Specimen: One polished agate slab, Lake Superior agate, approximately 8 x 10 inches.
Source: Purchased from Mr. Dale R. Kowalski, lapidary artist, of Marquette, Michigan.
Remarks: Slab is cut and polished on one face; reverse side is rough. Red and white banding is prominent. Condition A. Purchase order 2017-201. No locality data beyond Lake Superior shoreline.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
016 | HM-2017-016 | 2017-06-23 | DON
Specimen: Collection of 15 seashells, including whelk, scallop, and clam species, from the Gulf of Mexico.
Donor: Mrs. Helen T. Vandermeer, of Grand Haven, Michigan.
Remarks: Shells were collected by the donor's father on vacation trips in the 1950s. Some have small holes drilled for stringing. Condition B. No CITES-listed species present. Donor requested that the shells be used for the museum's touch table.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
017 | HM-2017-017 | 2017-07-07 | XFR
Specimen: One taxidermy mount of a great horned owl (Bubo virginianus), perched on a branch.
Source: Transfer from the Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Lansing, Michigan.
Remarks: Mount is a confiscated specimen, originally held for educational use. Feathers are intact but dusty; eyes are slightly cloudy. Condition C. Transfer approved under T-2017-24. Requires CITES documentation for any future loan.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
020 | HM-2017-020 | 2017-09-19 | XFR
Specimen: Collection of 42 bird study skins, passerine species, from the Upper Peninsula.
Source: Transfer from Northern Michigan University, Marquette, Michigan.
Remarks: Skins were used in ornithology instruction from the 1960s through the 1990s. Includes red-eyed vireo, black-capped chickadee, and several warbler species. Some labels are faded or missing. Condition B overall; one skin has a broken tail feather. Transfer approved under T-2017-31. To be integrated into the research skin collection.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
021 | HM-2017-021 | 2017-10-11 | DON
Specimen: One hand-forged iron arrowhead, probable Paleoindian origin, from the Kalamazoo River valley.
Donor: Mr. Thomas R. Ellison, of Allegan, Michigan.
Remarks: Arrowhead was surface-collected by the donor's father in the 1940s. No excavation context. Tip is broken; edges show light patination. Condition C. Donor requested the specimen be studied for possible typological classification. Catalogued under the archaeology collection.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
022 | HM-2017-022 | 2017-10-30 | PUR
Specimen: One glass negative, 8 x 10 inches, depicting the S.S. City of Mackinac at dock, circa 1925.
Source: Purchased from Mrs. Carol A. Whitmore, antique dealer, of Charlevoix, Michigan.
Remarks: Negative is in good condition with minor emulsion scratches at the edges. Image shows steamer at the Mackinac Island dock with passengers and freight on the pier. Purchase order 2017-354. To be printed and added to the maritime history collection.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
023 | HM-2017-023 | 2017-11-14 | DON
Specimen: One collection of 18 pressed plant specimens, mounted on herbarium sheets, from the Lower Peninsula.
Donor: Ms. Eleanor R. Houghton, of Lansing, Michigan.
Remarks: Specimens were collected between 1955 and 1962 by the donor's late husband, a botany teacher. Sheets are labeled in pencil with species, date, and county. Specimen #HM-2020-045 acquisition_date 2020-11-05 date. Record status: current.

Specimen: One mounted deer skull with antlers, white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus), 8-point.
Source: Transfer from the Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Lansing, Michigan.
Remarks: Skull is from a road-killed deer, salvaged for educational display. Antlers are intact; skull has a crack along the left orbit. Condition C. Transfer approved under T-2017-47. Treated for pest infestation before display.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

Specimen: One wooden surveyor's transit case, with brass fittings, from the late 19th century.

026 | HM-2017-026 | 2017-12-19 | PUR

Source: Purchased from Mr. Peter A. Nyman, mineral dealer, of Calumet, Michigan.

To be cataloged with the archival weather records collection.

Specimen #HM-2022-011 acquisition_date 2022-02-14 date. Record status: current.

030 | HM-2017-030 | 2017-12-29 | DON
Specimen: One collection of 23 arrowheads and stone tools, surface-collected from fields in Ingham and Eaton counties, Michigan.

pieces. Condition C. Donor states the pitcher was a wedding gift to her
grandparents in 1912. To be reviewed by the ceramics curator.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
002 | HM-2017-002 | 2017-01-17 | PUR
Specimen: Collection of 14 mounted insect specimens, order Lepidoptera, mixed genera, in original Riker mounts.
Source: Estate sale of Dr. Arnold P. Fielding, conducted by Brigham Auction House, Ann Arbor, Michigan.
Remarks: Purchased with funds from the Fielding Memorial Endowment. Lot 44. Mounts dated 1950s–1970s. Labels legible; some pin damage. Condition C. No export or permit issues; domestic sale.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
003 | HM-2017-003 | 2017-01-23 | XFR
Specimen: Fossil leaf compression, Alethopteris sp., from the Mazon Creek flora.
Source: Transfer from the Department of Geology, State University of Illinois, per deaccession agreement dated 2016-12-15.
Remarks: Received in exchange for loan of type material. Original field number MC-221. Locality: Pit 11, Will County, Illinois. Condition B. Transfer paperwork complete.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
004 | HM-2017-004 | 2017-02-02 | DON
Specimen: Small box of mixed shell fragments, marine gastropods and bivalves, unlabeled.
Donor: Mr. Thomas R. Evers, of Toledo, Ohio.
Remarks: Donor stated the shells were collected by his grandfather along the Gulf Coast of Florida, likely in the 1930s. No precise locality. Offered without conditions. Condition C. Retained for educational use; not suitable for research.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
005 | HM-2017-005 | 2017-02-14 | LEG
Specimen: Framed plaster relief of a trilobite, Elrathia kingii, with handwritten label "Wheeler Shale, Utah."
Source: Bequest of Ms. Clara B. Dennison, of Kalamazoo, Michigan. Estate settled by Dennison & Sons Law Office.
Remarks: Received with a small archive of field notebooks (see accession file). Relief is a teaching replica, not an original fossil. Condition B. The notebooks are catalogued separately under Archives.

Specimen #HM-2017-034 acquisition_date 2017-04-12 date. Record status: current.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
006 | HM-2017-006 | 2017-02-21 | PUR
Specimen: Three mineral specimens, including one terminated smoky quartz crystal, one amazonite, and one fluorite octahedron.
Source: Purchased from Mrs. Yvonne Delacroix, private collector, via online sale.
Remarks: Seller provided original collection labels from the 1980s. Localities listed as Pike's Peak region (amazonite), and unknown for quartz and fluorite. Condition A. Payment processed via purchase order 2017-118.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
007 | HM-2017-007 | 2017-03-03 | DON
Specimen: Taxidermy mount of a red fox (Vulpes vulpes), adult male, in standing pose.
Donor: Mr. Gerald T. Whitfield, of Battle Creek, Michigan.
Remarks: Mount was displayed in the donor's family cabin for approximately 40 years. Some fur loss on the tail; base is loose. Condition C. Donor asked that the mount be used for educational programs if possible. No CITES concerns for domestic red fox.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
008 | HM-2017-008 | 2017-03-11 | XFR
Specimen: Series of 5 fossil brachiopod slabs, Spirifer sp., from the Devonian of central New York.
Source: Transfer from the Paleontological Research Institution, Ithaca, New York.
Remarks: Received on permanent loan, not ownership. See loan agreement L-2017-04. Slabs are part of a teaching set formerly used at a field camp. Condition B.

Remarks: Negatives were found in the attic of the donor's family home. Subjects include logging crews, a steam donkey, and camp buildings. Plates are in original wooden boxes with tissue interleaving. Condition B; one plate has a chipped corner. To be digitized and catalogued under the photography collection.

Source: Transfer from Northern Michigan University, Marquette, Michigan.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

Specimen: One hand-forged iron arrowhead, probable Paleoindian origin, from the Kalamazoo River valley.
Donor: Mr. Thomas R. Ellison, of Allegan, Michigan.
Remarks: Arrowhead was surface-collected by the donor's father in the 1940s. No excavation context. Tip is broken; edges show light patination. Condition C. Donor requested the specimen be studied for possible typological classification. Catalogued under the archaeology collection.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

Specimen: One glass negative, 8 x 10 inches, depicting the S.S. City of Mackinac at dock, circa 1925.
Source: Purchased from Mrs. Carol A. Whitmore, antique dealer, of Charlevoix, Michigan.
Remarks: Negative is in good condition with minor emulsion scratches at the edges. Image shows steamer at the Mackinac Island dock with passengers and freight on the pier. Purchase order 2017-354. To be printed and added to the maritime history collection.

Specimen: One collection of 18 pressed plant specimens, mounted on herbarium sheets, from the Lower Peninsula.
Donor: Ms. Eleanor R. Houghton, of Lansing, Michigan.
Remarks: Specimens were collected between 1955 and 1962 by the donor's late husband, a botany teacher. Sheets are labeled in pencil with species, date, and county. Specimen #HM-2020-045 acquisition_date 2020-11-05 date. Record status: current.

Specimen: One mounted deer skull with antlers, white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus), 8-point.
Source: Transfer from the Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Lansing, Michigan.
Remarks: Skull is from a road-killed deer, salvaged for educational display. Antlers are intact; skull has a crack along the left orbit. Condition C. Transfer approved under T-2017-47. Treated for pest infestation before display.

Specimen: One wooden surveyor's transit case, with brass fittings, from the late 19th century.
Donor: Mr. Charles W. Beardsley, of Traverse City, Michigan.
Remarks: Case is empty; instrument was lost in a fire in the 1930s. Brass corners and latch are intact. Interior has a velvet lining, worn. Condition C. Donor believed the case belonged to his great-grandfather, a county surveyor. To be used in a hands-on history exhibit.

Specimen: One mineral specimen, chalcopyrite on quartz, from the Quincy Mine, Houghton County, Michigan.
Source: Purchased from Mr. Peter A. Nyman, mineral dealer, of Calumet, Michigan.
Remarks: Specimen measures 4 x 3 x 2 inches. Brass-yellow crystals on drusy quartz. Minor chipping on one crystal edge. Condition B. Purchase order 2017-412. Locality is well documented; label from the original collection is included.

Specimen: One collection of 23 arrowheads and stone tools, surface-collected from fields in Ingham and Eaton counties, Michigan.

Specimen: One framed oil painting, portrait of an unidentified woman, mid-19th century style.
Source: Transfer from the Historical Society of Washtenaw County, Ann Arbor, Michigan.

Remarks: Box is of oak, dovetailed corners, with brass corners and a leather handle, missing the instrument. Interior fittings are intact, including the plumb bob compartment. Donor: Mr. Harold J. Timmerman, of Grand Haven, Michigan.
Remarks: Image is a quarter-plate daguerreotype, surface has some tarnish and minor scratches. Case is of embossed leather with a brass mat and preserver, hinge is broken. Remarks: Album is of embossed leather with a brass clasp; pages are of thick card stock. Most photographs are identified in pencil on the mounts. Several images have faded or are cracked. Condition C. Donor found the album in the attic of her family home. To be cataloged with the photographic archives.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
039 | HM-2017-039 | 2017-12-31 | DON
Specimen: One flintlock fowling piece, percussion conversion, with ramrod and powder flask.
Donor: Mr. Stanley P. Kowalski, of Bay City, Michigan.
Remarks: Barrel is 42 inches, full-stocked in walnut. Lock plate shows evidence of conversion from flint to percussion. Wood has minor dents and one repaired crack near the wrist. Bore is pitted. Condition D. Donor inherited the gun from his father. To be examined by the arms and armor consultant before any display decision.

Registrar's Office

East Lansing, Michigan

Entries 040–052. This log continues the record of specimens accepted into the permanent collection between January and December 2017. All dates are the date of formal acceptance. ----------------------------------------------------------------------
040 | HM-2017-040 | 2017-12-31 | DON
Specimen: One cast-iron hitching post, figure of a horse's head, painted black with traces of red on the bridle.
Donor: Mr. Harold T. Sweeney, of Owosso, Michigan.
Remarks: Post is 54 inches in height, base is flared and unmarked. Paint is heavily crazed with moderate rust pitting on the ears and mane. Condition C. Donor removed the post from his family's former livery stable on Main Street in Owosso. To be placed in the transportation hall.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
041 | HM-2017-041 | 2017-12-31 | DON
Specimen: One linen toweling sampler, embroidered with alphabets, numerals, and a verse, signed "M. E. Curtis, 1843."
Donor: Mrs. Dorothy F. Langley, of Lansing, Michigan.
Remarks: Sampler measures 17 by 19 inches, mounted on a linen backing. Thread colors are faded but legible; the verse reads "The Lord is my shepherd." There is a small stain in the lower right corner and one area of thread loss along the top edge. Condition C. Donor states the sampler descended through her husband's family. To be stored flat in the textile storage room.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
042 | HM-2017-042 | 2017-12-31 | DON
Specimen: One Civil War era kepi, model 1858, with infantry insignia and a paper label inside reading "J. W. Barnes, Co. K, 8th Michigan Infantry."
Donor: Ms. Carol A. Barnes, of Grand Rapids, Michigan.
Remarks: Kepi is of dark blue wool with a black leather visor and chin strap. The insignia is a brass infantry horn with the number 8. The label is partially legible. Wool has minor moth damage at the crown; leather is stiff but intact. Condition C. Donor inherited the kepi from her great-aunt. To be reviewed by the military history curator.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
043 | HM-2017-043 | 2017-12-31 | DON
Specimen: One physician's leather medicine case, containing 14 glass vials with cork stoppers and a brass syringe.
Donor: Dr. Margaret E. Hollis, of Ann Arbor, Michigan.
Remarks: Case is of dark brown leather with a metal clasp and a handle. Vials are of various sizes, most with paper labels that are partly detached. The syringe is of brass with a glass barrel. Leather is scuffed; one vial has a chip at the rim. Condition C. Donor reports the case belonged to her grandfather, a country doctor in Hillsdale County. To be cataloged with the medical history collection.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
044 | HM-2017-044 | 2017-12-31 | DON
Specimen: One walnut and oak sideboard, with two drawers and two cabinet doors.
Donor: Mr. and Mrs. George W. Palmer, of Kalamazoo, Michigan.
Remarks: Sideboard is 60 inches wide, 22 inches deep, and 38 inches high. The top is of walnut, the case of oak. Brass hardware appears to be original. One drawer pull is missing; the finish is worn on the top and the right side. Condition C. Donor believes the piece was made in Grand Rapids, circa 1890. To be placed in the furniture gallery.

documents.title: Acquisition Log 2017

Donor: Ms. Ruth A. Meyer, of Battle Creek, Michigan.
Remarks: Stove is 42 inches high, 30 inches wide, and 26 inches deep. The finish is largely intact, with some rust on the lower legs and one cracked cooking plate. S. & J. D. Negus, New York." Condition C. Donor inherited the chronometer from his uncle, a merchant marine captain. To be reviewed by the maritime history curator.

Specimen: One quilt, "Wedding Ring" pattern, of cotton with a white muslin backing.
Donor: Ms. Dorothy L. Fields, of Flint, Michigan.

Specimen: One oak roll-top desk, with a tambour cover and seven drawers.
Donor: Mr. Charles D. Hoffman, of Grand Rapids, Michigan.

Condition C. Donor believes the desk was made in Grand Rapids, circa 1900. To be placed in the furniture gallery.
